text: Private management tends to be more efficient than public management, so healthcare should be provided by private operators with public funding.
Public-Private Partnerships are not a useful instrument for the country, even when they are well negotiated and supervised.
Generous unemployment benefits discourage people from looking for work and starting businesses, and often end up doing more harm than good in the long run.
There are several infrastructures and companies that should remain public because they are strategic for the country's sovereignty.
It is crucial to keep public debt under control, even if that means cuts to public investment, public-sector wages and social spending.
Reducing employment protection would give firms more incentive to hire, boosting the economy and job creation.
The government should use tax incentives to steer consumption or investment decisions towards strategic goals, even if this makes the tax system more complex.
The government should use taxes and environmental regulations to fight climate change.
Economic regulation protects consumers and workers, but it is often excessive, stifling the economy and entrepreneurship.
In general, the private sector makes better investment decisions than the State, which rarely knows where to allocate resources effectively.
Personal income tax should be less progressive in order to attract and retain talented people with higher incomes and better qualifications.
As a rule, cutting corporate income tax has little positive impact on investment and on the economy's international competitiveness.
Large inheritances should be taxed because heirs have no merit in receiving that income.
Subsidies targeted at those most in need can often create dependency on the State and be counterproductive in the long run.
As a rule, as the tax burden increases, economic activity is increasingly discouraged.
In most circumstances, free trade improves the well-being of all countries involved.
The European economy remains too fragmented and should converge towards a true single market in order to compete with the United States and China.
The European Union should take geopolitical and strategic considerations into account instead of trading freely with all countries, regardless of their values and policies.
If a once-strong national industry suffers from international competition, the State should support or protect it.
Working and setting up businesses in any EU country should be easier, even if that means giving up some control over national economic and labour laws.
Recreational use of cannabis should be banned.
Prostitution should be legalised and regulated.
Euthanasia should be banned.
Societies should give more weight to animal welfare, even when it threatens national traditions.

It is essential that schools teach children about the diversity of human experience — including issues such as racial, gender or sexual discrimination — in order to build a fairer and more empathetic society.
Equality of opportunity between sexes and ethnicities is not enough; equality of outcomes must be guaranteed, namely through permanent quotas in the public and private sectors.
Religion should be kept entirely out of public schools.
The State should be tolerant towards minority religions in the country.
The Church plays a positive and important role in society, so it should not pay taxes.
Having a dominant and culturally relevant religion is crucial for a country's social cohesion.
Having communities with different cultures in the country enriches society without undermining the national culture.

Immigration should be easy, because the vast majority of immigrants seek to build a better life for themselves, in harmony with the native population, and because they contribute positively to the country.
It is not right to stigmatise a social group, even if a minority of that group is associated with improper or illegal behaviour.
Immigrants should be required to learn the language of the host country, even if they abide by its laws.
Immigrants should not have the same legal and civic rights as the native population.
Investing in technological progress (such as clean energy, energy efficiency and electric vehicles) — not reducing consumption — is the best way to fight climate change and protect the environment.
The social impact of social media is more negative than positive.
The social costs of artificial intelligence will far outweigh its benefits.
We should invest in Genetically Modified Organisms (GMOs) and explore other forms of genetic engineering.
Europe should invest more in nuclear energy.
The separation of political powers is more important than the speed of political decision-making.
Sustainable social and political progress comes from strong, enlightened leaders, not from dialogue and compromise between the different parts of society.
It is essential that a democracy has strong checks and balances between the different powers, even if this makes the political system more complex and opaque and accountability harder to establish.
It is important that civil servants are protected from political pressure, even if this makes public administration reforms more difficult.
My country's political system needs a profound overhaul, since its political institutions cannot be reformed and improved.
The constitution should protect individual rights without discriminating against minorities, regardless of the will of the majority.
The government should try to regulate the media to ensure that fake news does not spread.
The main goal of the prison system should be to punish severely in order to deter crime, not to rehabilitate offenders.
Freedom of expression should be protected even when it distresses oppressed minorities or authority figures, or is directed against national symbols, as long as it does not incite violence.
Some freedoms should never be compromised, not even temporarily, and not even in the face of extraordinary events (such as a war or a pandemic).
It is more important to ensure that criminals and corrupt people are caught and punished than to ensure that innocent people are not unjustly prosecuted or convicted.
The European Union should not help liberal democracies against aggression by autocratic countries, whether economically or by providing military support.
The best way to resolve complex diplomatic issues such as the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is for the international community to empower international organisations such as the United Nations.
Economic sanctions are a good way to condemn foreign-policy acts we disagree with and to promote the country's values internationally.
Military alliances with countries that share similar values, such as NATO, are the best way to ensure lasting peace, even if that means being dragged into a war in the worst-case scenario.
Joining the European Union was beneficial and further European integration is desirable, even if it implies a greater transfer of national sovereignty.
Being part of a stronger European Union would benefit my country in the long run, even if in the short run it may bring costs in some areas, such as agricultural and fisheries policy.
It is possible to find solutions to problems such as climate change and international tax evasion through national policies, without international cooperation and political integration.
Issuing common European debt is an important and desirable step for future European integration.
Developed nations do not have a moral obligation to take in refugees fleeing their country because of issues such as war or climate change.
